Subject: Production: sudden throughput drop despite reserved capacity

Evelyn —

We are seeing a sharp drop in throughput and sustained latency increases from our FinSys production traffic starting ~08:45 PST today. Our dashboards show that the reserved GPU pool attached to our account reports 100% utilization but requests are queuing and a lot of requests are getting 500 errors. This is impacting trading models and is urgent.

Attached: finsys_error_log_0819.txt (sample error traces), pool_util_dashboard_0819.png (high-level metrics).

Can you confirm this is on your side and what you can do to restore baseline throughput? Our SRE is standing by.

—Samir
Samir Singh
Head of Platform, FinSys

Samir —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachments. I'm escalating this to our infra on-call (cc'd). Initial ask: can you share a short window (start/end) for a concrete example request id from today? That will let us reconcile traces. In parallel Marcus will pull pool-level KPIs.

- Marcus to validate whether the pool is saturating (GPU/PCIe/SMX) vs. a software-level queueing point.

On Wed, Aug 19, 2026 at 09:23 AM evelyn_hart wrote:
> Samir —
> 
> Thanks for the quick heads-up...

I pulled the pool metrics and traces for FinSys (pool id: finsys-pool-77). Summary of findings:

- GPU utilization: SM utilization ~95%, but NVLink/PCIe stalls increased sharply starting 08:38 PST.
- Queueing: request queue length jumped due to a small cohort of long-context generation jobs that kept KV cache pinned; these blocked efficient batching for the rest of traffic.
- Error profile: 500-class errors are concentrated on one serving node (node-77b) with repeated OOM/retry cycles.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:30–09:35):
1) Evacuated traffic away from node-77b and restarted the worker processes on that host.
2) Enabled emergency burst (non-dedicated) capacity and routed a portion of FinSys traffic to the burst pool to relieve pressure.
3) Applied an interim throttle for long-context jobs in your account (max-concurrency reduced from 40 -> 12) to reduce KV pressure while we stabilize.

Impact: queue length decreased ~70% in 20 minutes, p95 latency improved from ~1.8s to ~0.7s for majority of requests; errors reduced but not eliminated. Remaining work:
- Rebalance reserved allocation to reduce single-node hotspots (root cause appears to be uneven shard placement).
- Investigate kernel-level PCIe stalls with infra team; may require a rolling host reprovision.

Next steps: Marcus + infra to run a prioritized rolling update tonight (02:00–03:30 UTC) with expected 30–45 minute intermittent capacity reduction; we'll coordinate a narrower maintenance window.

I'll paste a short dashboard link and attach a draft mitigation plan.

—Marcus Lin
Senior Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime

Evelyn / team —

Thanks for the updates and for executing the mitigations. We've seen p95 and error rates return to acceptable levels over the last 12 hours. The rolling update last night caused a brief maintenance period (we lost ~25 capacity-minutes during the window) but the rebalances look promising.

Procurement: the 10% credit is acceptable as a starting gesture — we'll await the formal credit note and the post-mortem.

A couple of asks from us:
- Please confirm whether the underlying cause (shard placement + KV cache pressure) has a code or scheduler change targeted, and the ETA.
- We need a guarantee in writing that reserved accounts will have a prioritized fallback route (traffic steering) if a single-node hotspot forms again.

Samir
